title: Quick quiz: how efficient appliances work
intro: Ten questions on the technology. Tap an answer to see why.
messages: Worth another read of the guide above.

qs.q: How does an induction cooktop heat a pot?
options: A magnetic field heats the pan itself
A hot coil under the glass
qs.why: The cooktop surface stays cooler than the pan.

qs.q: Will your pans work on induction?
options: Yes, if a magnet sticks to the bottom
qs.why: Cast iron and many stainless pans work. Copper and aluminum alone do not.

qs.q: How does a heat pump dryer differ from a regular dryer?
options: It recycles its air and needs no outside vent
qs.why: It dries clothes using a heat pump that captures and reuses heat, so it uses much less energy.

qs.q: What does ENERGY STAR Most Efficient mean?
options: A top tier among ENERGY STAR certified models
A model with no electricity use
qs.why: It marks the best performers each year.

options: A new one uses much less electricity
qs.why: Fridges have improved a lot. Replacing an old one can cut a noticeable share of your bill.
They use less water per load, so there is less water to heat and less to dry.

qs.q: Is it efficient to run a full dishwasher?
options: Yes, often more than washing the same dishes by hand
qs.why: Modern machines use little water per load.

qs.q: Where does most of a washing machine's energy go?
qs.why: A cold-water cycle on a modern detergent saves most of that.

qs.q: What does the yellow EnerGuide or EnergyGuide label show?
options: Estimated yearly energy use and cost
qs.why: It lets you compare models on running cost, not just price.

qs.q: Why use a range hood vented outdoors?
options: It removes moisture and cooking pollutants
qs.why: Cooking adds steam and fine particles to indoor air, whatever the fuel.
